My formula is =PMT(0.06/12, 60, -10000) for a hypothetical 10,000 loan at 6% over five years, and it returns 193.33, which matches the loan calculator on the MoneyHelper website. But when the term cell contains text like "5 years" I get #VALUE!, and when I test a 0% rate in my homemade version, =P*r/(1-(1+r)^-n), it shows #DIV/0!. Is there a clean way to make the formula handle a zero rate, and should I use an IF with a simple division for that case? I'd also like a column showing total interest paid over the term.
